Part of the near hull wall is deliberately removed as a clean museum-model cutaway, exposing repeated tall structural ribs, deep cargo holds, a mountain of thousands of individually folded rust-red and dark iron-ore paper pellets; above them the real deck and closed hatch covers continue. This is clearly an explanatory model of the loaded ship, not damage or a hole in a sailing ship. The intact forward pilothouse rises over a tiny generic paper deckhand for human scale, rigging, ladders, winches, weathered plates and careful seams. Strong warm industrial grazing light across red ore, cool slate lake and subdued shore behind, deep shadows between ribs. Make the ore and interior structural repetition the focus, rather than a tiny vessel on a horizon. Two substantial cream card labels physically supported at the cutaway base, exact English text: 'IRON ORE' and '26,000+ TONS'. Readable typeset letters in perspective, no additional editorial copy or invented archive. All cargo/gravity and structural support plausible. Ship intact above cutaway; quiet loaded state, no storm, no depiction of sinking.
